newsitem.title: UK: New Wall St peak boosts weak Euro bourses.
newsitem.headline: New Wall St peak boosts weak Euro bourses.

text.p: Wall Street surged to an intra-day trading record on Monday, giving an end-of-the-day boost to European bourses which had been in the doldrums because of interest rates uncertainties.

In currency markets, the dollar, which weakened last week after a strong run, fell to two-month lows against the mark with traders predicting little in U.S. economic data due this week to re-ignite the rally.

On equity markets, all eyes were on Wall Street which closed at its third consecutive high on Friday. Shortly after opening on Monday, the Dow Jones average shot up to 6251.50 points, eclipsing the previous intra-day peak, also set last Friday.
The surge gave European stocks a late push. London was lifted from the minus column to end the day ahead and Amsterdam was nudged into record territory at the close.
Amsterdam's AEX index of 25 blue chips closed 4.39 points percent higher at 597.10, beating the previous best of of 594.33 set on October 18.

Dealers said the Dutch market shrugged off a slightly weaker dollar, normally a bearish factor for Amsterdam. "The lower dollar didn't seem to hurt us at all and that indicates that there just aren't any sellers," said one dealer.

In London, Europe's biggest bourse, shares languished in negative ground for most of the day because of worries over interest rates. "London is painting itself into a corner with these worries about domestic interest rates," said one.
But Wall Street's sharp advance delivered a mild lift enabling the stocks to rally, finishing up 3.6 points.
Whether the eleventh-hour rally in London would carry over into Tuesday was questionable as investors were largely preoccupied with domestic inflation and interest rate worries.

"The prospect of further interest rate rises, fears of a politically-motivated Budget, and the impact of strong sterling on international earners are all likely to hinder performance for the next few weeks." said Ian Williams, strategist at Panmure Gordon.

But some analysts said the jitters over interest rates and inflation were overdone. They saw the market mood improving once it was clear that 1997 would offer better growth with continued low inflation.
In Frankfurt, floor trading, which ends before Wall Street's opening, closed down 0.4 percent in thin trading as investors took profits from Friday's record highs on the DAX bourse.
The Dax index, closed at 2728.32 points down 11.51, with the weaker dollar depressing the market.
The Paris bourse was closed for a national holiday commemorating the end of World War One.
The dollar weakened to two-month lows against the mark in Europe as currency traders took profits in thin trading.
"What we're seeing is some profit-taking in a very thin market, which has triggered some stops below 1.50," said a UK bank dealer. "People don't seem to have turned dollar negative yet."
Holidays in currency markets in the United States and elsewhere kept activity to a minimum, and the lack of liquidity exaggerated some of the dollar's moves, said dealers.
Against the yen, the dollar was also weak. Currency traders were awaiting Japanese indicators due on Tuesday and U.S. figures late in the week.
"The yen is likely to continue to push upwards ahead of the machinery orders data out tomorrow and the EPA's (Economic Planning Agency) report," said Julian Fisher, economist at Daiwa Europe.
CURRENCIES AT 1715 GMT
The dollar was at 1.4975 marks and 111.04 yen, compared with 1.5045 marks and 111.60 yen in late European trade on Friday.
STOCK MARKETS CLOSING PRICES
The Financial Times-Stock Exchange index of 100 leading British shares ended 3.6 points higher at 3,914.4.
The French share market was closed for a national holiday celebrating the armistice of World War One.
The 30-share DAX index in Frankfurt closed down 11.51 at 2,728.32.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold ended at $380.75 an ounce, compared to $378.95 at the close on Friday. Silver was $3.87, up six cents.
